terms.term: Wells with no recent production that are not plugged, wells with no recent production and no responsible operator, or wells that have been plugged to prevent migration of gas or fluid.
Part of production; boosting equipment is used to compress, dehydrate, and sweeten natural gas after it has been extracted from underground.
Part of downstream activities; the delivery of oil and natural gas from major pipelines to the end users.

The last step of the oil and gas supply chain, which consists of refining oil into useable products and distribution of the final oil and gas products, including the local distribution of natural gas.

The process of burning excess natural gas at the production well using a dedicated flare to ignite the methane and other components in the gas, which can result in both methane and carbon dioxide emissions (CO₂).
Part of production; gathering pipeline systems gather crude oil and natural gas from production wells.
A potent greenhouse gas that is released from oil and gas activities and has extreme effects on climate warming.
The middle step of the oil and gas supply chain, which consists of transportation and storage of oil and gas and processing of gas.
The U.S. oil and natural gas industry encompasses the production of raw oil and gas from wells to the delivery of processed oil and gas to consumers.
Midstream step in which water, impurities, and other light hydrocarbons are removed from raw natural gas to produce pipeline grade natural gas, also called dry natural gas.
Part of upstream activities; involves extracting oil and natural gas from underground.
Part of downstream activities; involves converting crude oil into gasoline, diesel fuel, and jet fuel.
A part of natural gas processing in which hydrogen sulfide and carbon dioxide, acidic gases often found in the raw gas, are removed.
A downstream activity; transmission pipelines transport the refined petroleum products and processed natural gas to city gate stations or industrial end users.
The first step in the oil and gas supply chain, which consists of exploration and production of oil and gas resources, including gathering and boosting.
The direct release of natural gas into the atmosphere, typically in small amounts.
